what_it_does: This chip converts very high-frequency radio signals (millimeter-wave frequencies used in 5G and radar) into digital bits that a computer can process. The challenge is capturing extremely fast signals spanning a 38 gigahertz bandwidth while maintaining clean, undistorted data. Rather than sampling at the final RF (radio-frequency) rate, the chip uses a clever trick called sub-sampling—it samples at a lower rate but in a way that still captures the full RF content through aliasing. The design achieves this in a modern small technology (22nm) with careful attention to the sampling window, anti-aliasing filters, and noise performance across the 1 to 32 gigahertz band.
